values.condition: Total velocity of the candidate high-velocity star J1443+1453 discovered by Huang et al. (2021), as quoted in this paper; probably originating from Sgr

evidence.quote:
Recently, Huang et al. (2021) discover a candidate HVS (J1443+1453) with a total velocity of
559 km\mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }that is probably from Sgr.

notes: J1443+1453: previously reported as a candidate HVS and reanalyzed here (T:p2-b2, T:p8-b3). The paper's 60-star Sgr-origin sample is not individually identified in the supplied materials; its v_GC > 0.75 v_esc threshold (T:p4-b6) is a high-velocity selection, not an explicit Galactic-unbound criterion. The two HVS noted within that sample (T:p1-b8, T:p5-b5) have no individual names or source IDs, so they cannot be listed separately.

J1443+1453: J1443+1453 is not one of the 60 sample stars; it is the candidate from Huang et al. (2021) that the authors re-test (T:p8-b3, Figure 1/2). For this star the paper additionally reports minimum distance to Sgr Δr_min = 3.33_{-0.51}^{+1.09} kpc, trace-back time t_trace = 39.4_{-3.2}^{+2.6} Myr, and star-Sgr velocity difference Δv = 665_{-30}^{+43} km/s from their own analysis, plus Huang et al. values Δr_min = 2.42_{-0.77}^{+1.8} kpc, t_trace = 37.8_{-6.0}^{+4.6} Myr and Δv = 690_{-65}^{+104} km/s (T:p8-b3). These are not among the requested quantity definitions (Δv is a velocity relative to Sgr, not the heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity or total Galactic-rest-frame speed). The 559 km/s total velocity is attributed to Huang et al. (2021) as quoted in the text. No right ascension, declination, parallax, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is explicitly reported for this star; only its approximate location (r_GC ≈ 7.5 kpc, v_GC ≈ 500 km/s) can be read from Figure 1 (I:p6-b0), which is not tabulated.
